messages.author: 4e1046f70a71bb2d
messages.subject: Poor heritability alternatives
parts:
Hello,

I am excited to implement this method and I have a few questions!

I am interested in specifying a latent Alzheimer's disease factor in a two or three factor model. I believe including amyloid in some capacity would be valuable; however, I have not found any gwas summary stats for amyloid measures (plasma, CSF, nor PET/autopsy) that meet the > 4 heritability z score recommendation. They all have low heritability around 2. 

Since amyloid is biologically relevant, I would like to include amyloid in some capacity.

Is it possible that in the gwas where amyloid is defined as amyloid positive or negative (not a continuous value), could the assumed population prevalence used for liability-scale conversion substantially influence the estimated SNP heritability or its z score?

Alternatively, would it be reasonable to define the other latent factors using traits with sufficiently strong heritability and then include the Alzheimer’s disease-related traits, such as amyloid, as observed outcomes in structural regressions? If so, how problematic would a low heritability z score be for interpreting these regression estimates? Would it primarily reduce precision, or could it also make the genetic covariance and regression estimates unreliable?

Thank you for your help!

messages.author: ac421cf36d1a4c37
messages.subject: Re: Poor heritability alternatives
parts:
while the h2 liability estimate depends on the assumed prevalances, its Z statistic does not. A Z cutoff for h2snp of 4 is conservative. You can certainly bring it down to 2, keeping in mind that power will be more limited, CIs will be wider, and estimates may be less stable. Note that for AD and very closely related phenotypes, ldsc likely automatically detects and excludes the top associated variants in the APOE region to protect against them exerting undue leverage on the ldsc slope. We prefer to exclude the APOE region entirely so that we can more cleanly interpret the h2snp as indexing common variant polygenic signal outside of the APOE region. The de la Fuente PLOS genetics paper is a good resource for that approach and related issues surrounding analysis of polygenic variation relevant to AD risk. 
https://journals.plos.org/plosgenetics/article?id=10.1371/journal.pgen.1010208#sec002
